2610.13678.title: Retractions Revisited: A Replication, Extension, and Mechanistic Evaluation of Linguistic Obfuscation Effects in Fraudulent Science
2610.13678.paper_summary: Prior work suggests fraudulent scientists write their articles with higher rates of linguistic obfuscation than genuine scientists, with a possible mechanism suggesting obfuscation makes research more costly for a reader to analyze. This result has not undergone additional empirical scrutiny in the open science era, nor have other psychological mechanisms been evaluated. The current replication and extension addressed this opportunity by comparing 800 fraudulent and 800 genuine control papers (2013-2025). The results supported the linguistic obfuscation hypothesis, suggesting fraudulent papers were more obfuscated than genuine ones. A parallel mediation model evaluated three competing mechanisms, finding that reality monitoring, as measured through decreased rates of adjectives, best explained the link between fraudulent science and linguistic obfuscation. Cross-validated detection accuracy using obfuscation features (60.7%) and an elastic net of over 100 language dimensions (71.6%) were significantly greater than chance. Implications for scientific fraud and psychology of language research are discussed.
2610.13678.paper_summary_zh: 先前的研究表明，欺詐性科學家的文章在語言模糊性方面的寫作比真實科學家更高，可能的機制表明模糊性使得讀者分析研究的成本更高。這一結果在開放科學時代尚未經過進一步的實證檢驗，其他心理機制也未被評估。本次複製與擴展研究利用800篇欺詐性論文和800篇真實控制論文（2013-2025）來填補這一機會。結果支持了語言模糊性假說，表明欺詐性論文的模糊性高於真實論文。一個平行中介模型評估了三個競爭機制，發現現實監控（通過形容詞使用率的降低來衡量）最佳解釋了欺詐性科學與語言模糊性之間的聯繫。使用模糊性特徵的交叉驗證檢測準確率（60.7%）和超過100個語言維度的彈性網（71.6%）顯著高於隨機機率。本文討論了對科學欺詐和語言心理學研究的影響。
2610.13678.author: David M. Markowitz et.al.
